title: Performance and acting
purpose: Direct what a character shows and what they hide, so a keyframe or clip prompt carries behaviour instead of a single emotion label.
use_cases: Writing `performance.surface` and `performance.hidden` per shot: smiling (surface) while afraid of being found out (hidden).
Choosing one micro-behaviour per beat (a held breath, a glance away, hands that stop moving) instead of a bigger face.
Giving a voice take an intention (to reassure, to stall, to provoke) before choosing pitch or pace.
Keeping a character fingerprint: the habits and posture that stay the same across episodes.
anti_patterns: One emotion word per shot ('sad') pasted into the prompt; the face goes generic and the same in every shot.
Hidden emotion that repeats the surface one, so there is no subtext to play.
Gaze that wanders with no target; eyelines must point at someone or something in the set.
Dialogue with no pauses; silence before a line is often where the acting is.
An expression sized for the look, not by default: live-action-like looks shrink the move as the shot gets closer, while anime looks may push a close-up reaction on purpose. Decide it per look.
Emotional jumps between adjacent shots with no event in between (the trajectory breaks).

checks.measure: a shot with `performance.hidden` names a different emotion from `performance.surface`
reviewer marks the gaze target in the first, middle and last frame
reviewer lists each shot's surface emotion in order and names the event behind each change
the user says whether the character feels like themselves
